items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The sitar is a plucked Hindustani instrument with movable curved frets, a gourd resonator and extra 'sympathetic' strings that ring along. Pandit Ravi Shankar made it famous worldwide.

distractors.d: The Saraswati veena has a second gourd near the top and a broader body.
distractors.a: The sarod has no frets and a smooth metal fingerboard.
distractors.b: The tanpura has no frets; it only plays a drone.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The Saraswati veena is the main plucked instrument of Carnatic (South Indian) music. Look for the second resonator gourd near the scroll-shaped top.

distractors.d: The sitar has one main gourd and curved movable frets.
distractors.a: The tanpura has no frets.
distractors.b: The santoor is a flat box struck with mallets.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The sarod is fretless: the player slides along a polished metal fingerboard. Its body is covered with goat skin. Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a famous sarod player.

distractors.d: The sitar has frets and a much longer neck.
distractors.a: The sarangi is bowed and has a boxy shape.
distractors.b: The ektara has just one string on a bamboo frame.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The santoor is a hammered string instrument from Kashmir, struck with light walnut-wood mallets. Pandit Shivkumar Sharma brought it into classical music.

distractors.d: The harmonium has a keyboard and bellows.
distractors.a: The jal tarang is a set of bowls with water.
distractors.b: The sarangi is bowed, not struck.

items.stem: Name this pair of drums.
items.explanation: The tabla is a pair: the smaller wooden 'dayan' for the right hand and the larger 'bayan' for the left. The black spot (syahi) gives its ringing tone. Ustad Zakir Hussain was a world-famous tabla player.

distractors.c: The mridangam is one long drum with two heads.
distractors.d: The dholak is a single barrel drum played on both sides.
distractors.a: Nagaras are large kettle drums played with sticks.

items.takeaway: Two separate drums, black spots = tabla.

items.stem: Name this drum.
items.explanation: The mridangam is the main percussion instrument of Carnatic music, played on both ends with the hands. Its North Indian cousin is the pakhawaj.

distractors.a: Tabla is a pair of separate drums.
distractors.b: The damaru is a small hourglass-shaped drum.
distractors.c: The djembe is a goblet-shaped African drum.

items.stem: This clay pot is played as an instrument in Carnatic concerts. What is it called?
items.explanation: The ghatam is a specially fired clay pot played with fingers, palms and wrists. Pressing its mouth against the stomach changes the tone.

distractors.a: The kanjira is a small frame drum.
distractors.b: The tabla has skin heads.
distractors.c: Not the name of this classical instrument.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The shehnai is a double-reed wind instrument heard at weddings and temples. Ustad Bismillah Khan made it a classical concert instrument and received the Bharat Ratna.

distractors.d: The bansuri is a bamboo flute with no bell or reed.
distractors.a: The pungi has a gourd and two pipes.
distractors.b: Bagpipes have a bag and several pipes.

items.stem: This long wind instrument is played in South Indian temples and weddings. What is it?
items.explanation: The nadaswaram is one of the loudest non-brass acoustic instruments, usually played with the thavil drum at South Indian temples and weddings.

distractors.c: The shehnai is the shorter North Indian cousin.
distractors.d: A bansuri is a flute, with no reed or bell.
distractors.a: The clarinet is a Western single-reed instrument with metal keys.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute linked with Lord Krishna. Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is its best-known master.

distractors.d: The shehnai has a reed and a flared bell.
distractors.a: A recorder is blown from the end, not the side.
distractors.b: Algoza is a pair of flutes played together.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The sarangi is a bowed instrument carved from a single block of wood. It is said to copy the human voice closely, so it often accompanies singers.

distractors.d: The sarod is plucked, not bowed.
distractors.a: The violin has a curved body and a long fingerboard.
distractors.b: The sitar is plucked and has a long neck.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: 'Ek tara' means 'one string'. It is played by Baul singers of Bengal and many folk musicians.

distractors.d: The tanpura has four or more strings.
distractors.a: The sarangi is bowed and has many strings.
distractors.b: The santoor has many strings and is struck.

items.stem: This instrument plays only a continuous background drone, not a melody. What is it?
items.explanation: The tanpura's strings are plucked one after another to give a steady drone that singers and players tune to.

distractors.d: The sitar plays melodies and has frets.
distractors.a: The veena plays melodies and has frets.
distractors.b: The sarod plays melodies.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The hand-pumped harmonium came to India from Europe in the 1800s and became central to bhajans, qawwali and film music.

distractors.d: The santoor has strings and mallets.
distractors.a: A piano is far bigger and uses hammers on strings.
distractors.b: The accordion is strapped on and squeezed with both arms.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: 'Jal tarang' means 'waves in water'. The amount of water in each bowl sets its pitch.

distractors.d: The ghatam is a single clay pot.
distractors.a: The santoor has strings.
distractors.b: A xylophone uses wooden bars.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: The pungi is a folk wind instrument known from snake charmers. One pipe plays the drone, the other the tune.

distractors.d: The shehnai is a single pipe with a bell.
distractors.a: Bagpipes have a bag, not a gourd.
distractors.b: The bansuri is a plain bamboo flute.

items.stem: This long wooden wind instrument comes from which country?
items.explanation: The didgeridoo was developed by Aboriginal peoples of northern Australia. Players use circular breathing to keep a continuous drone.

distractors.a: Not its origin.
distractors.b: Japan's bamboo flute is the shakuhachi.
distractors.c: Not its origin.

items.stem: Name this musical instrument.
items.explanation: Bagpipes are strongly linked with Scotland. The player fills the bag with air and squeezes it to feed the pipes. Indian army bands play them too.

distractors.d: The accordion has keys and pleated bellows.
distractors.a: The pungi has a gourd, not a bag.
distractors.b: The trumpet is a brass instrument with valves.

items.stem: This goblet-shaped hand drum comes from which region?
items.explanation: The djembe comes from West Africa (the old Mali Empire region). It is played with bare hands.

distractors.d: Not its origin.
distractors.a: Not its origin.
distractors.b: Not its origin.

items.stem: This carved stone wheel belongs to which temple?
items.explanation: The 13th-century Konark Sun Temple in Odisha is built as a giant chariot of the Sun god with 24 carved wheels pulled by stone horses. The wheel appears on the ₹10 note (2018 series).

distractors.a: Hampi has a stone chariot, but this wheel is from Odisha.
distractors.b: Known for colourful gopurams.
distractors.c: Known for its tall spires and sculpture.

items.stem: Where is this famous stone chariot?
items.explanation: The stone chariot is a shrine to Garuda in the Vittala temple complex of Hampi, the capital of the Vijayanagara empire. It appears on the ₹50 note (2018 series).

distractors.c: Konark is itself shaped like a chariot, but this standalone shrine is in Hampi.
distractors.d: Known for its rathas carved from single rocks.
distractors.a: Known for Hoysala temple carving.

items.stem: This richly carved stepwell is…
items.explanation: Rani ki Vav in Patan, Gujarat, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site with hundreds of carved sculptures. It appears on the ₹100 note (2018 series).

distractors.d: A stepwell too, famous for its zigzag steps.
distractors.a: A palace screen wall, not a well.
distractors.b: A domed tomb.

items.stem: This dome-shaped monument with carved gateways is the…
items.explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi (Madhya Pradesh) was begun by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE. Its four toranas are carved with Buddhist stories.

distractors.d: A tomb with a huge dome, no toranas.
distractors.a: A modern building shaped like a lotus.
distractors.b: A square monument with four minarets.

items.stem: This huge domed tomb, famous for its whispering gallery, is…
items.explanation: Gol Gumbaz in Vijayapura (Bijapur), Karnataka, is the tomb of Mohammed Adil Shah. A whisper under its dome can be heard across the gallery.

distractors.c: White marble with four separate minarets.
distractors.d: Red sandstone on a raised platform in a garden.
distractors.a: Looks like a smaller Taj Mahal.

items.stem: This lotus-shaped building is in which city?
items.explanation: The Lotus Temple is a Bahá'í House of Worship in Delhi, designed by architect Fariborz Sahba and opened in 1986. It is open to people of all faiths.

distractors.b: Not here.
distractors.c: Not here.
distractors.d: Not here.

items.stem: This pink building with many small windows is…
items.explanation: The Hawa Mahal ('Palace of Winds', 1799) let royal women watch street life unseen. Its jharokhas (small windows) also let breezes cool the building.

distractors.a: A large palace with domes.
distractors.b: A domed palace of golden-yellow sandstone.
distractors.c: A white palace by a lake.

items.stem: This monument with four minarets is in which city?
items.explanation: The Charminar ('four minarets') was built in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah and is the symbol of Hyderabad.

distractors.a: Lucknow has the Bara Imambara and Rumi Darwaza.
distractors.b: Agra has the Taj Mahal.
distractors.c: Bijapur has the Gol Gumbaz.

items.stem: This cloth painting with fine lines and decorative borders is…
items.explanation: Pattachitra ('cloth picture') from Odisha is painted on treated cloth with natural colours, often showing Jagannath and stories from the epics.

distractors.d: Warli uses simple white stick figures.
distractors.a: Gond fills shapes with dots and lines.
distractors.b: Kalighat uses quick bold brush strokes on paper.

items.stem: This painting fills animals and trees with dots and lines. Which art form is it?
items.explanation: Gond art comes from the Gond community of Madhya Pradesh. Artist Jangarh Singh Shyam brought it to national attention.

distractors.c: Madhubani fills space with double outlines and motifs, mainly from Bihar.
distractors.d: Pichwai shows Shrinathji on cloth.
distractors.a: Tanjore uses gold foil and raised gesso.

items.stem: This painting style with bold, quick brush strokes developed near a temple in Kolkata. It is…
items.explanation: Kalighat paintings were made in the 1800s near the Kalighat Kali temple, quickly painted with watercolours for visitors, and often commented on society.

distractors.a: Pattachitra is finely detailed.
distractors.b: Phad is a long scroll from Rajasthan.
distractors.c: Warli is white on mud background.

items.stem: This painting with gold foil and raised decoration is from which style?
items.explanation: Tanjore paintings from Tamil Nadu use gold foil and gesso (chalk paste) relief, with deities as the main subject.

distractors.a: Related, but it uses thin gold work and less relief.
distractors.b: No gold foil; from Bihar.
distractors.c: Pen-drawn and dyed fabric.

items.stem: These large cloth paintings of Shrinathji hang behind the deity in Nathdwara. They are called…
items.explanation: 'Pichwai' means 'at the back'. These hangings from Nathdwara, Rajasthan, change with seasons and festivals.

distractors.c: Phad is a scroll about folk heroes like Pabuji.
distractors.d: Pattachitra is from Odisha.
distractors.a: Kalamkari is from Andhra Pradesh.

items.stem: This long painted scroll, unrolled while singers tell the story of a folk hero, is…
items.explanation: Phad paintings from Bhilwara, Rajasthan, are performed at night by bhopa singers. They often tell the story of Pabuji or Devnarayan.

distractors.d: Pichwai is a temple hanging of Shrinathji.
distractors.a: Kalighat is on paper and from Bengal.
distractors.b: Gond is a Madhya Pradesh tribal art.

items.stem: This fabric's pattern of tiny dots is made by tying the cloth before dyeing. What is it called?
items.explanation: In Bandhani (from 'bandh', to tie) small points of cloth are tied tightly with thread so dye can't reach them. It is a craft of Gujarat and Rajasthan.

distractors.d: Ajrakh is block-printed.
distractors.a: Phulkari is embroidery.
distractors.b: Chikankari is white embroidery.

items.stem: This silk with blurred-edge geometric patterns is woven using double ikat. It is…
items.explanation: In Patola from Patan, Gujarat, both warp and weft threads are tie-dyed before weaving (double ikat), so the pattern is the same on both sides.

distractors.b: Kanjeevaram uses a heavy zari border, not ikat.
distractors.c: Bandhani is tie-dyed after weaving.
distractors.d: Ilkal is known for its pallu and border.

items.stem: This bright 'flower work' embroidery comes from which state?
items.explanation: Phulkari ('flower work') is darned on the back of the cloth with floss silk in bright colours.

distractors.a: UP's Lucknow is known for Chikankari.
distractors.b: Karnataka's embroidery is Kasuti.
distractors.c: Bengal's embroidery is Kantha.

items.stem: This delicate white embroidery is a craft of which city?
items.explanation: Chikankari is traditionally white-on-white embroidery from Lucknow, using many stitch types such as shadow work.

distractors.a: Jaipur is known for block prints and blue pottery.
distractors.b: Known for silk sarees.
distractors.c: Known for Ajrakh and mirror work.

items.stem: This block-printed cloth in indigo and red, from Kutch, is…
items.explanation: Ajrakh is printed with carved wooden blocks using resist and natural dyes (indigo, madder) through many washing stages. It is made in Kutch and Sindh.

distractors.a: Bagru is a Rajasthan block print with earthy colours on lighter grounds.
distractors.b: Kalamkari is pen-drawn and from Andhra Pradesh.
distractors.c: Bandhani is tie-dyed dots.

items.stem: This heavy silk saree with a contrasting gold border is named after a town in which state?
items.explanation: Kanjeevaram sarees come from Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu. The body and border are often woven separately and joined.

distractors.a: UP's Varanasi makes Banarasi silk.
distractors.b: Gujarat's silk is Patola.
distractors.c: Assam makes muga and eri silk.

items.stem: This tubular steel chair from the Bauhaus was designed by…
items.explanation: Marcel Breuer designed the Wassily chair (1925) at the Bauhaus, reportedly inspired by bicycle handlebars. It showed how industrial steel tube could make light furniture.

distractors.c: They worked with moulded plywood and plastic.
distractors.d: A much later French designer.
distractors.a: He designed the Red and Blue chair.

items.stem: This chair is a famous example of which design movement?
items.explanation: Gerrit Rietveld's Red and Blue chair (around 1918–23) uses primary colours and straight elements, like a Mondrian painting turned into 3D.

distractors.a: Art Nouveau uses flowing curves.
distractors.b: Memphis is 1980s and playful, not a strict grid.
distractors.c: Arts and Crafts favoured handmade natural wood.

items.takeaway: Primary colours + straight lines = De Stijl.

items.stem: Who designed this famous lemon squeezer for Alessi?
items.explanation: Philippe Starck's Juicy Salif (1990) is often discussed as an object people buy for its sculpture-like form more than its function, which makes it a classic debate on form vs function.

distractors.c: Rams designed simple Braun products.
distractors.d: Breuer designed tubular steel furniture.
distractors.a: Panton designed plastic furniture.

items.takeaway: Juicy Salif = Starck; form vs function.

items.stem: What made this chair a design breakthrough?

options.text: It is a single piece of moulded plastic, cantilevered with no back legs
It folds flat into a box
It is hand-carved from one tree

items.explanation: Verner Panton's chair (designed 1960, produced from 1967) was one of the first chairs moulded from a single piece of plastic.

distractors.c: It doesn't fold.
distractors.d: It's moulded plastic.
distractors.a: It has no mechanism.

items.stem: This chair with an X-shaped steel frame was designed by…
items.explanation: Mies van der Rohe (with Lilly Reich) designed it for the 1929 Barcelona International Exhibition. Mies also said 'Less is more'.

distractors.a: He designed other steel-tube chairs, but not this.
distractors.b: Eames worked mainly with plywood and plastic.
distractors.c: Rams designed electronics and shelving.

items.stem: This lounge chair and footstool of moulded plywood and leather were designed by…
items.explanation: The Eames Lounge Chair (1956) shows their mastery of moulded plywood. The Eameses also wrote the India Report that led to NID.

distractors.c: Known for steel-tube chairs.
distractors.d: Known for the Juicy Salif.
distractors.a: Known for the Red and Blue chair.
